Hi Jessica — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (our Private deployments lead) and Aditya (runtime networking) to validate the checklist and provide a concise runbook.

Quick answers up front:
- Splunk HEC: supported via HTTPS egress to a customer-managed HEC endpoint inside your VPC (we can support mutual TLS or token-based HEC).
- TLS & cert rotation: we support customer-supplied certificates and automated rotation via your KMS/HSM; there is also a short-term option for cert pinning during POC.
- Egress rules: we'll provide IP ranges and port set, plus guidance for NAT/gateway setups for air-gapped sites.

Thanks both — I reviewed the attached spreadsheet. I'm attaching a short diagram and a proposed validation checklist. High-level notes below, followed by the checklist.

High-level approach we recommend for AcmeHealth POC:
1) Export channels supported:
   - HTTPS -> Splunk HEC (preferred for structured app logs & events)
   - Syslog over TLS -> Splunk forwarder (if you prefer collector-based ingest)
   - OTLP/gRPC -> internal observability forwarder -> SIEM (for trace/span telemetry; requires an internal collector)
2) Authentication & certs:
   - HEC token is supported; for higher assurance enable mTLS using customer certs.
   - We can integrate with your KMS for cert rotation; we publish a cert rotation API and a sample automation script.
3) Network considerations:
   - Egress ports: 443 (HEC/TLS), 6514 (syslog-TLS), 4317 (OTLP/gRPC) if you use direct OTLP.
   - IP allowlist: recommend allowing our egress gateway IP pool (we'll provide a CIDR list) or peer via private link.
   - For air-gapped environments: use our local forwarder (agent) to write to an internal collector; we provide transfer bundle/manifest for manual transfer.

Attached checklist (summary):
- Verify HEC endpoint + token or mTLS certs
- Configure egress rule to REDWOOD_EGRESS_CIDR over 443
- Ensure TLS validation with customer root and rotation schedule
- Enable request sampling header to preserve trace context and include correlation IDs in logs
- Validate event schema through small batch (10K events) and check field mapping in Splunk indexes

Attachments: onprem_export_diagram_v2.png, redwood_private_export-runbook.pdf

Marissa Cole
Product Infrastructure Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Quick technical addendum from networking/runtime:
- If Acme prefers outbound-only, we recommend HEC over HTTPS with token + client-side cert validation. We'll supply a small egress proxy binary (container) that performs batching, retry, and backpressure to preserve SLOs.
- For network allowlisting: provide a /28 pool for the POC. Production will need broader ranges; we can support private link peering for zero-egress-flow.
- Trace hooks: we inject X-Redwood-Trace and keep the KV cache mapping for trace continuation. For OTLP paths, the forwarder will convert spans to your collector format and add the necessary enrichment (customer_id, environment).
- Audit logs: we can provide a signed audit bundle for compliance review (events about export configuration changes).

I'll follow up with the CIDR list and a config snippet for the egress proxy by EOD.

- Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
